# Decoded edges respect the parts

**Claim.** If a perfect-matching code decodes only into pairs from different parts, its generated graph is a subgraph of the complete multipartite graph.

**Proof.** To show the subgraph relation, take any adjacency in the graph generated by the decoded pairs. By the pair-list adjacency characterization (`pairListGraph_adj_iff`), either the ordered pair or its reversal occurs in the decoded list. The code's partite condition, together with the fact that $k>0$, ensures that the two endpoints of every decoded pair lie in different parts (`decodedBookPartiteEdge_parts_ne`). Reversing the endpoints preserves that inequality. Hence every edge of the generated graph is an edge of the complete multipartite graph.

**Key facts.** `FABL.pairListGraph_adj_iff`, `FABL.decodedBookPartiteEdge_parts_ne`.
